title: Functional annotation of parasitic worm genomes, by assigning protein names and GO terms
protocol: Identify one-to-one or many-to-one orthologues for each predicted gene in the genome of interest in human, zebrafish, Drosophila melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans, and Schistosoma mansoni using an in-house database of gene families.
Check if the predicted gene of interest has a manually curated protein name in UniProt for human, zebrafish, Drosophila melanogaster, or C. elegans orthologues.
Check if the predicted gene of interest has a manually curated protein name in GeneDB for S. mansoni orthologues.
Download correspondence between UniProt accessions and Ensembl accessions from the UniProt website if Ensembl accessions were used in the in-house database of gene families.
Select an orthologue from _C. elegans_.
If no orthologue in _C. elegans_, select from _S. mansoni_.
If no orthologue in _S. mansoni_, select from human.
If no orthologue in human, select from _D. melanogaster_.
If no orthologue in _D. melanogaster_, select from zebrafish.
Use the UniProt ‘recommended name’ (RN) if orthologue is from UniProt.
Use the GeneDB ‘product description’ if orthologue is from GeneDB.
Check for an orthologue with a non-curated protein name from TrEMBL if no curated names are found.
Transfer the selected protein name from step 4 or 5.
Record the UniProt/GeneDB accession of the source protein and the evidence code ECO:0000265.
Number genes if several are assigned the same protein name due to many-to-one orthology.
Run InterProScan version 5.0.7 on the protein sequences for all predicted genes in the query species.
Assign a protein name based on InterPro domains if no protein name is assigned by orthologues.
Note the InterPro accession of the source domains and record the evidence code ECO:0000259.
If a query protein is not assigned a name based on either orthologues or InterPro domains, name it ‘Hypothetical protein’.
Add the protein names to the protein fasta file headers for the species of interest.

Identify one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many orthologues for each predicted gene in the genome of interest in human, zebrafish, _Drosophila melanogaster_, and _Caenorhabditis elegans_ based on an in-house database of gene families.
Download manually curated GO annotations for human, zebrafish, _C. elegans_, and _D. melanogaster_ from the Gene Ontology website.

Filter downloaded GO annotations to retain only those with evidence codes IDA/IEP/IGI/IMP/IPI, excluding annotations with a ‘NOT’ qualifier or to the term GO:0005515 (‘protein binding’) based on criteria used by the Compara project for projecting GO terms to vertebrate orthologues.
Download the GO hierarchy from the Gene Ontology website.
Check whether the predicted gene of interest has human, zebrafish, _Drosophila melanogaster_, or _Caenorhabditis elegans_ orthologues with manually curated GO terms.
Take each pair of orthologues from two different species.
Use a breadth-first search algorithm to find the last common ancestors of their GO terms in the GO hierarchy.
Find the last common ancestors for all combinations of GO terms between the two orthologues.
Calculate the union of all last common ancestors found for each orthologous pair.
Remove any GO term that is an ancestor of another term in the set within the GO hierarchy.
Note the UniProt accession of the source orthologue protein for each GO term.
Record the evidence code for the GO term as IEA (‘inferred from electronic annotation’).
Assign GO terms of molecular function, cellular component, and biological process types to each query protein.
Identify GO terms using InterproScan, which identifies InterPro domains in the protein and maps GO terms to the domains.
Note the InterPro accession(s) of the source domain for each identified GO term.
Record the evidence code for the GO terms as IEA (‘inferred from electronic annotation’).
